project.researchNotes: Sequential place 7 of 14. Strict settlement merit, See, café-led Eat, all named trail providers, picnic, public visitor parking, public toilets, access, transport, dogs and complete local HES/NRHE construction dates were checked before continuing. The Dory and Larachmhor Tavern are meal-led and removed from Eat. Festival-only pop-ups are not treated as dependable year-round facilities.

touristAppeal.label: Strong Destination
touristAppeal.summary: Pittenweem remains a strong working-harbour and arts destination with historic fabric, tidal pool, coastal walking and a live treasure trail. Its Eat list is now restricted to true café, sweet-treat and refreshment stops.
touristAppeal.dogAccessSummary: The harbour, West Braes, coast path, Treasure Trail and several outdoor or dog-welcoming food stops make a strong visit with a dog. The cave and gallery do not publish general pet access, however, so the dog-owner score is five points lower rather than being boosted by friendliness.

visitorHighlights.name: Pittenweem Working Harbour and Wynds
visitorHighlights.reason: An authentic commercial fishing harbour tightly integrated with steep historic wynds and food stops.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Open-air public waterfront; daylight visit recommended. Harbour operates Mon–Fri 06:30–21:00.

editorialReview.scoreRationale: A distinctive, active and visually coherent working harbour with several linked reasons to linger.

visitorHighlights.name: West Braes, Tidal Pool and Crazy Golf
visitorHighlights.reason: A useful cluster of coast-path scenery, play, crazy golf, refreshments and tidal swimming rather than one isolated facility.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Park and tidal pool always accessible; hut and crazy golf seasonal and volunteer-dependent.
visitorHighlights.admission: Park and pool free; crazy golf charges apply.

editorialReview.scoreRationale: Good outdoor breadth and strong coast-path fit, reduced for tidal swimming risk and volunteer-dependent facilities.

visitorHighlights.name: St Fillan’s Cave
visitorHighlights.reason: A genuinely unusual key-access cave beneath Cove Wynd, albeit compact and physically constrained.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Key available from the Cocoa Tree during café opening hours; verify before travel.

editorialReview.scoreRationale: Unusual and atmospheric local history, reduced for small scale, uneven access and dependence on a third-party key holder.

visitorHighlights.name: Weem Gallery and Framer
visitorHighlights.reason: A year-round changing-exhibition gallery that gives Pittenweem’s art identity a permanent, visitable anchor.

editorialReview.scoreRationale: A credible year-round expression of Pittenweem’s art identity, reduced for modest scale and no published dog policy.

suggestedFirstVisit.title: Link harbour, cave and West Braes
suggestedFirstVisit.summary: Start at the working harbour, climb Cove Wynd for St Fillan’s Cave and the High Street, then finish west along the coast at West Braes.

townGuide.visitorMood: More layered than its size suggests: a real fishing harbour, intimate streets, distinctive food and art, and easy access to the coast all reinforce one another.

North wall is mainly of 17th century date, rubble-built.

features.licence: Open Government Licence v3.0; retain Historic Environment Scotland attribution.
features.fullDescription: Dated 1635, re-faced late 19th century, early to earlier 20th century shopfront. Prominent crowstepped 2- and 3-storey with attic, 4-bay, T-plan former merchant's house in irregular terrace (adjoining separately listed late 16th century town house of Earls of Kellie), and with single storey and attic, red sandstone, pantiled projection at rear. Painted lined render. Painted base course, deep band course over ground floor. S (HIGH STREET) ELEVATION: chamfered arrises to door at centre. Banded surround to bipartite window at right (E). Moulded architraved windows at 1st and 2nd floors, all with advanced cills; broad 6-panelled centre door with large window (now bipartite) below modern fascia at right and well-detailed shop (see below) to left. Regularly-fenestrated bays at each floor above, 1st floor with bipartite window at outer left and moulded date panel at centre over modern plaque worded 'THE OLD MANSE'; 2nd floor with smaller windows abutting eaves. Tall, 2-bay gable to centre of rear elevation with lower red sandstone projection at right extending into higher ground. SHOPFRONT: geometric-tiled lobby and decoratively-etched part-glazed door at left with display window to right over deep stallriser, all under multi-pane clerestorey with coloured vertical lights and 3 panels, centre panel worded 'TEAS'. Blind box with outer handles and centre locking strip below modern fascia (see Notes). 9- and 12-pane glazing patterns in replacement timber sash and case windows. Grey slates and red clay pantiles. Ashlar stacks, that to E truncated and with thackstane. INTERIORS: some good interior detail retained including moulded cornices, architraves, panelled timber doors and shutters, timber fire surrounds with cast iron grates. Encaustic tiled hall floor and dog-leg staircase with boarded timber dado. Shop retains part-glazed timber panelling, counter and shelves.

features.fullDescription: Andrew Haxton, 1913. Single storey T-plan school with lower single storey flat-roofed projection to S. Harled, base course, some stone mullioned and transomed windows, gable-headed windows breaking eaves, some segmental. S (PRINCIPAL) ELEVATION: symmetrical. Central 3-bay section with central tripartite window breaking eaves enclosing carved panel, 'PITTENWEEM PUBLIC SCHOOL ERECTED 1913' flanked by segmental-gabled single light windows with long stylised keystones. Flat-roofed front projection (now painted cream): inner 2-bay section with tripartite window flanked by 3-light canted bay windows. At outer bays, slightly recessed 1-bay section with oculus flanked by recessed single bay piended sections with gabled bipartites with re-entrant angle containing entrance doors. W ELEVATION: central 2-bay section with gabled windows breaking eaves, to right very advanced single bay piended section with off-centre gabled window. To left, advanced single bay piended section with central gabled window. E ELEVATION: mirror image of W elevation. N ELEVATION: slightly advanced entrance with stylised keystone above flanked by segmental-headed single light windows. Door to far right with 4 steps set at right-angles. Predominantly timber sash and case windows with horns, 8-pane over 2-pane. Hopper windows to upper parts of transoms. 2-leaf timber doors to W, E and N with margined glass panels above. Those to W and E with top-curved fanlight above. Graded grey slates. Corniced ridge stack to N of W elevation. INTERIOR: very good complete interior with few alterations. Large assembly hall with decorative pierced roof vents. Timber boarding to dado. Doorcase to N contains memorial to First and Second World Wars. Predominantly timber 3-panel doors with margined glass panels above with original handles. Classrooms mostly as built. Room to NW contains black range with white tiles set into white tiled area. To left, fitted timber bookcases with margined glass panels above. GATE PIERS AND BOUNDARY WALLS: predominantly brick with flat coping to W, N and E. Simple square brick gate piers to W. To S, very low outer wall surmounted by railings curves inwards to simple square gate piers with corniced caps. Simple pier to outer right. High rubble wall with triangular coping runs S to N forming courtyard entrance to school.
